cases.sentence: Пройдя коридор, фельдшер ввел Ростова в ___, состоявшие из трех, с растворенными дверями, комнат.
cases.explain: «офицерские палаты» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Going along the corridor, the assistant led Rostóv to the officers’ wards, consisting of three rooms, the doors of which stood open. There were beds in these rooms and the sick and wounded officers were lying or sitting on them. Some were walking about the rooms in hospital dressing gowns. The first person Rostóv met in the officers’ ward was a thin little man with one arm, who was walking about the first room in a nightcap and hospital dressing gown, with a pipe between his teeth. Rostóv looked at him, trying to remember where he had seen him before.

cases.sentence: — Вот где Бог привел свидеться, — сказал ___.
cases.explain: «маленький человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “See where we’ve met again!” said the little man. “Túshin, Túshin, don’t you remember, who gave you a lift at Schön Grabern? And I’ve had a bit cut off, you see …” he went on with a smile, pointing to the empty sleeve of his dressing gown. “Looking for Vasíli Dmítrich Denísov? My neighbor,” he added, when he heard who Rostóv wanted. “Here, here,” and Túshin led him into the next room, from whence came sounds of several laughing voices.

cases.sentence: В лице его была та же бледная опухлость, которая была на всех ___.
cases.explain: «гошпитальных лицах» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: His wound, though a slight one, had not yet healed even now, six weeks after he had been hit. His face had the same swollen pallor as the faces of the other hospital patients, but it was not this that struck Rostóv. What struck him was that Denísov did not seem glad to see him, and smiled at him unnaturally. He did not ask about the regiment, nor about the general state of affairs, and when Rostóv spoke of these matters did not listen.

cases.sentence: Денисов не расспрашивал ни про полк, ни про ___ дела.
cases.explain: «общий ход» — after the preposition «про», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: Он, казалось, старался забыть ту прежнюю жизнь и интересовался только своим делом с ___.
cases.explain: «провиантскими чиновниками» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Rostóv even noticed that Denísov did not like to be reminded of the regiment, or in general of that other free life which was going on outside the hospital. He seemed to try to forget that old life and was only interested in the affair with the commissariat officers. On Rostóv’s inquiry as to how the matter stood, he at once produced from under his pillow a paper he had received from the commission and the rough draft of his answer to it. He became animated when he began reading his paper and specially drew Rostóv’s attention to the stinging rejoinders he made to his enemies. His hospital companions, who had gathered round Rostóv—a fresh arrival from the world outside—gradually began to disperse as soon as Denísov began reading his answer. Rostóv noticed by their faces that all those gentlemen had already heard that story more than once and were tired of it. Only the man who had the next bed, a stout Uhlan, continued to sit on his bed, gloomily frowning and smoking a pipe, and little one-armed Túshin still listened, shaking his head disapprovingly. In the middle of the reading, the Uhlan interrupted Denísov.

cases.sentence: Госпитальные товарищи Денисова, окружившие было Ростова — вновь прибывшее из ___ лицо, — стали понемногу расходиться, как только Денисов стал читать свою бумагу.
cases.explain: «вольного света» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
